zone: B01d Rm 2170 (open-office bullpen, Unit 4 Lvl 2) - VAV 04B038FEC on JacksonLabs tree
description: Low-airflow complaint: Zone temp 71.5F above cooling SP 70.6F (calling for cooling). Supply Damper Command 100%, Supply Air Damper Position visually confirmed true full-open after recalibrating a mis-clamped Johnson Controls M9208-GGA-3 actuator (had a 30% dead-zone offset). Despite full-open damper, Supply Flow tops out ~400cfm against 805cfm setpoint. Flow-vs-command curve shows classic diminishing returns: 30%->300cfm, 55%->369cfm, 70%->385cfm - rules out actuator/calibration as root cause. Veris Dry Pressure transmitter reads 0.1 in.wc (genuinely low velocity, not a sensor fault). Conclusion: real physical restriction or AHU capacity limit upstream of the box, isolated to this branch or AHU-wide - not a controls/actuator problem.

zone: B01d Rm 2170 - Johnson Controls M9208-GGA-3 actuator
action: Visually verified supply air damper blade at true full-open; found actuator mis-clamped with a 30% dead-zone offset and recalibrated it.
outcome: Damper now genuinely full-open at 100% command, confirmed by direct visual inspection - but flow still caps ~400cfm vs 805cfm setpoint, so the dead-zone was a real but secondary fault. Root cause is upstream (duct restriction or AHU capacity), see same-day research entry.

zone: B01d Rm 2170 - AHU identity research (Z:\Duct Prints, hvac/data/metasys_points.json, hvac/data/building_maps_index.md)
description: Metasys tree shows box on AHU-1-1 with no confirmed AHU-1E tag; colleague guessed AHU-10 (unconfirmed). Resolved via cross-reference: metasys_points.json topology_quirks already documents B1 AHU-14 as object 04B016FEC on JL-BLDG57-SNE04/FC-B. Rm 2170 VAV object 04B038FEC is the same 04B0xx range on the same trunk - strong structural match to AHU-14, not AHU-1E (that tag is real but serves Unit 5/Bioinformatics per Z:\Duct Prints\B01 E\Mechanical.pdf, Project 2882.63) and not AHU-10 (no B1 AHU-10 exists anywhere in metasys_points.json - only a B21 AHU-10, different building). Confirmed physically: Z:\Duct Prints\B01 D\Feed From AHU14\MH101.pdf (1st floor) and MH102.pdf (2nd floor), WBRC Project 2882.38, AS-BUILT 11-28-03, "Jackson Laboratory Unit 4 Renovation" ductwork plans - MH102 shows Rm 2170 by name on the same sheet as VAV-12/VAV-13 (open office 2085) and the 2135-2195 office row incl. 2185. MH101 shows the riser to 2nd/3rd floor near VAV-11/VAV-14 with a note to rebalance the rooftop exhaust fan (Penn DX16VSR) to maintain 2nd/3rd floor CFM - all branches on this 2003 as-built run 100-400cfm, well under the 805cfm now demanded by Rm 2170. The 2007 renovation (Unit4.3rdFloorReno_06.02, Project 288247) touched telecom/video-conf/graphics/mailing offices elsewhere on the floor, NOT the 2075-2200 corridor - so this branch is confirmed still running original/never-upsized 2003-vintage ductwork, consistent with the diminishing-returns flow curve (undersized branch, not equipment fault). Sibling boxes for AHU-wide vs. isolated-branch comparison: VAV-11, VAV-12, VAV-13, VAV-14 (named on MH101/MH102, same AHU-14 feed).

zone: B01d Rm 2170 - physical duct sizing check
description: Measured branch duct diameter at ~10in round near the VAV box. At 805cfm design flow this works out to ~1476 fpm, which is a normal/acceptable design velocity for a 10in duct (typically sized for ~1500fpm) - this duct is correctly sized for the 805cfm setpoint on paper. This REVISES the working theory: undersized 2003-vintage branch ductwork is likely NOT the root cause (at least not at this measured point). With sizing ruled out, the leading theory shifts to a localized restriction along the run - a kink, crushed section, partially-closed manual volume damper (VD), or bad elbow/transition geometry - or an AHU-14 capacity/static-pressure limitation. Still need to: (1) measure duct size at 2-3 more points along the run toward the main trunk to rule out a narrower section elsewhere, (2) check AHU-14 discharge static pressure and fan speed directly in Metasys (04B016FEC).

zone: B01d Rm 2170 - end-of-day summary written for Wayne discussion
description: Wrote hvac/data/rm2170_low_airflow_summary.md consolidating the full days investigation for an in-person discussion with Wayne. Key unresolved point: AHU identity is NOT conclusively settled - drawings show 3 different air handlers (AHU-14, AHU-1E, AHU-3) with documented ties to Unit 4 Second Floor, and none of the paper trail confirms which reaches Rm 2170/2185/2187 specifically. AHU-10 is ruled out (no B1 AHU-10 exists). Duct measured at 10in round near the box, correctly sized for 805cfm - rules out blanket undersizing, narrows theory to a localized restriction (kink/crush/closed VD) or an AHU-wide static/capacity limit. See summary doc for full open-questions list and next steps.

zone: B01d Rm 2170 (MaintainX WO #400557, Rm #2165/EDU Suite Cubicle Area) - manual volume damper, Rm 2178
action: Found the actual restriction: a manual hand volume damper (VD) serving the 2170 branch, physically located in Room 2178, was set to roughly 50% open. Opened it to 75%.
outcome: RESOLVED (pending client follow-up). Box flow reached setpoint immediately after opening the damper; zone is actively cooling down. This confirms the leading theory from the days investigation: a partially-closed manual balancing damper upstream of the box was the actual restriction, NOT AHU-14/AHU-1E/AHU-3/AHU-10 capacity or duct sizing (10in branch duct was already confirmed correctly sized). The VAV boxes own damper being 100% open the whole time was real but was never going to fix this - the restriction was upstream, exactly as theorized after the duct-sizing check ruled out a blanket undersizing explanation. Confirmed with client (Lily Schenk) that airflow will be noticeably louder in the suite going forward; she is OK with this and will flag if it becomes a problem. Plan to check back with client later this week to confirm noise is acceptable and temp has actually come down.
